question: Should OpenClaw ship AG-UI as a bundled channel with its own HTTP/authentication surface and two new runtime dependencies, rather than wait for a general external-channel direction?
rationale: The implementation is a new core-distributed channel, config surface, and gateway security boundary; repository policy reserves that scope decision for maintainers even though existing bundled channels provide a partial structural precedent.

options.title: Sponsor bundled AG-UI
options.body: Approve the bundled-channel direction, then require exact-head dependency authorization and packaged-install proof before merge.

options.title: Defer for an external-channel seam
options.body: Pause this PR until maintainers choose and document a general external-channel packaging and discovery model.

options.title: Decline core distribution
options.body: Close the proposal if the project does not want to own this protocol, its dependencies, and its gateway attack surface in the core release.

recommendation.title: Sponsor bundled AG-UI
recommendation.body: Approve the bundled-channel direction, then require exact-head dependency authorization and packaged-install proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: This contributor has the clearest available history for the imported implementation and its package-distribution repairs, though a core channel or security owner should make the decision.
